call_points.text: No numeric revenue or margin guidance; management only said greenfields should contribute to the bottom line in one or two quarters.
Q1 revenue grew 37%, of which 7% was copper inflation; the rest volume, content, premiumisation and new model launches.
EVs contributed 8.5% of Q1 revenue; company is engine-agnostic across ICE and EV platforms.
NCR minimum wages rose 30-40%; the mandated increase is fully reflected in Q1 results, other states not concluded.
Employee cost was INR600 crores in the quarter; management declined to quantify the wage-hike portion separately.
Greenfield plants held revenue at about INR450 crores run rate and break-even, same as the previous quarter.
FY27 budgeted capex will be funded from internal accruals.
Wage pass-through talks with customers have no timeline; management would not commit to a share of the impact recovered.

operating_notes.text: EV revenue share is 8.6% for Q4FY26 and 6.6% for 12MFY26.
Greenfield plants at Kharkhoda, Pune, and Navagam are at varying utilization levels, generating over ₹400 crores quarterly.
Copper pass-through lag remains 3-6 months, with a 7% delta unrecovered in Q1FY27 versus 17% in the preceding quarter.
Greenfield plants ran at about INR450 crores quarterly revenue and break-even, flat on the previous quarter.
EVs were 8.5% of Q1FY27 revenue; management targets ROCE above 40%.
The company has no reportable segments as CODM reviews operations as a whole.

timeline.summary: Vivek Chaand Sehgal, Promoter, declared no encumbrance on Motherson Sumi Wiring India shares by promoters or promoter group as of March 31, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹3,334.62 Cr (+32.9% YoY), net profit ₹167.3 Cr (+1.4% YoY).
Motherson Sumi Wiring reported Q4FY26 revenue of ₹3,335 Cr (+32.9% YoY) and net profit of ₹167 Cr.
Motherson Sumi Wiring reported Q4FY26 revenue of ₹3,335 Cr (+32.9% YoY) and net profit of ₹167 Cr, crossing ₹10,000 Cr annual revenue for the first time.
Motherson Sumi Wiring held its Q4 FY26 earnings call reporting annual revenues crossing ₹10,000 crores.
On its Q1FY27 call (Aug 4, 2026), MSWIL said revenue grew 37% with 7% from copper inflation, EVs were 8.5% of revenue, and NCR minimum wages rose 30-40%, fully absorbed in the quarter.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹4,053.83 Cr (+46.8% YoY), net profit ₹223.37 Cr (+35.1% YoY).

watchlist.response: Management said the increase was significant and fully in the results but declined to quantify it or give a pass-through timeline, calling it a matter between the company and customers.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked how much of the NCR minimum-wage hike was in the INR600 crore employee cost and when customers would compensate.

watchlist.response: Management declined plant-level profitability, saying to look at the company overall, and gave no Pune-specific utilisation figure.
watchlist.text: Analysts pressed for greenfield plant-level margins and utilisation, including the Pune plant.
